entities.summary: El Padre del Tango — 'El Choclo' (1903), 'La Morocha' (1905), first tango recordings in Philadelphia
Afro-Argentine — composed 'El Entrerriano' (1897/98), first tango published in musical notation
Afro-Argentine — 'father of tango', formed first documented tango ensemble with El Mulato Sinforoso
Uruguayan — composed 'La Cumparsita' (1916), most famous tango ever written
El Tigre del Bandoneón — died alone in Paris at 32
Established piano in tango orchestra; first 'La Cumparsita' recording (1916); ~3,000 recordings
Coined 'Orquesta Típica Criolla' (1910) — set the template for tango orchestras
Afro-Argentine payador — explicitly linked milonga to candombe: 'milonga was the daughter of African Candombe'
Harmonically ahead of his time — 'Qué noche', 'Tinta verde', 'Lorenzo'
Most legendary early tango dancer — bridges Guardia Vieja to Golden Age
Most important nucleus of Afro-Uruguayan culture — demolished by military dictatorship Dec 3, 1978 (now National Day of Candombe)
African-derived drum music — foundation of tango's rhythm; three drums: chico, repique, piano
Cuban-born rhythm that became foundational to tango — dotted 2/4 pattern with syncopated bass
entities.definition: Despite the name ('from Havana'), the habanera's syncopated character derives from the African tresillo rhythm. Traveled route: Africa → Cuba → Spain → Río de la Plata.

entities.summary: The cultural figure who mediated between rural criollo world and immigrant city — 'a gaucho who had unsaddled'
entities.definition: Young man of modest social condition inhabiting Buenos Aires outskirts. Descended from gauchos who came to city as frontier closed. Brought rural milonga and payada traditions into urban tango.

entities.summary: 1913 called 'the year of the tango' — Pope banned it, Kaiser forbade officers, tango conquered anyway
Close embrace master, 'an orchestra in his head'
The Last Compadrito, philosopher of tango
The King of the Milonga, self-taught genius
Most flamboyant milonguero, Graciela González's mentor
Danced the phrase, not the rhythm. Gravedigger by trade.
A monument of ideas made into movement. Died dancing.
Co-creator of Villa Urquiza style with Milonguita
La Leona del Tango, creator of first Followers Technique seminar (1994)
Tete's partner from 1995, musicalizadora, continues teaching internationally
Maestros of the maestros, trained multiple World Champions
Keeper of traditional technique, 30+ years studying with masters
The minimalist - knows dozens of steps but doesn't use them
Authority on canyengue, revived the oldest tango style
Canyengue researcher and practitioner with Luis Grondona; co-founded Mo.C.C.A. (2002)
2004 World Champions, 'Honey Feet' - returned after 30 years
Pepito Avellaneda's wife and dance partner
Danced to age 98, never traveled internationally
Sweethearts reunited after 30 years, married twice
Respected milonguera, beautiful footwork, never traveled internationally
Never left Buenos Aires, still dancing in his 90s
Co-creator of Villa Urquiza style with El Turco José
UNESCO-listed birthplace of Villa Urquiza style
UNESCO-listed, Carlos & Rosa's home base
Downtown milonga, Tete's last dance was here
Historic downtown salon, featured in BBC documentary
Intimate milonga, home of Ismael Heljalil and milonguero style
Major milonga venue, exhibitions by Pocho & Nelly
Upright posture, long elegant steps, created 1945-56 by Milonguita & El Turco
Close embrace, shared axis, born in crowded downtown clubs of 1950s
Oldest tango form (1890s-1920s), bent knees, African-Argentine roots
From the edges of Buenos Aires, playful and rhythmic, working-class roots
Invitation to dance by eye contact and subtle head nod
entities.definition: Traditional method of inviting a partner to dance using eye contact and a small nod. Ensures no public rejection and maintains the codes of the milonga.

entities.summary: Set of 3-4 songs of same style, danced with one partner
entities.definition: A set of 3-4 songs by one orchestra or in one style, danced with the same partner. Separated by cortinas which signal it's time to change partners.

entities.summary: Musical interlude between tandas signaling partner change
entities.definition: Short musical interlude (usually non-tango music) played between tandas to signal dancers should thank their partner and return to their seats.

entities.summary: The unwritten social codes and etiquette of the milonga
entities.definition: The elaborate unwritten rules governing milonga behavior: cabeceo for invitations, counter-clockwise navigation, no teaching on the floor, proper dress. Violations can mean expulsion.

entities.summary: Stacked/leaning embrace with shared axis
entities.definition: A close embrace technique where partners share their axis with a slight forward lean toward each other. Core element of milonguero style dancing.

entities.summary: Interrupted ocho, invented when space ran out
entities.definition: A 'cut' or interrupted ocho figure. Legend says it was invented when a milonguero started an ocho, realized he lacked space, and cut the move short.

entities.summary: Counter-clockwise flow of dancers around the floor
entities.definition: The counter-clockwise flow of dancers around the perimeter of the dance floor. Maintaining the ronda is essential floorcraft and part of the códigos.

entities.summary: The King of the Beat — returned tango to danceable 2/4 rhythm in 1935
Elegant, melodic 'walking' music — the purest expression of tango
Perfect synthesis of rhythm and emotion — the musician's musician
Last survivor of Big Four — imprisoned by every regime, red carnation defiance, cooperative orchestra; kept tango alive through Decadencia; created 'La Yumba' (1946)
Wizard Hands — staccato piano style, off-beat accents
Explosive combination with Alberto Castillo — 'Así se Baila el Tango'
Orquesta de las Estrellas — refined elegance, school of stars
Glostora Tango Club — 22 years on radio, 486 recordings
Born Uruguay, added double bass 1917; 3,792 recordings — tango's greatest entrepreneur
63-year career, 1,250+ recordings — aristocratic style, introduced vibraphone
Voice of tango — 800+ recordings, UNESCO Memory of the World, created tango canción with 'Mi noche triste' (1917), 8 Paramount films; 'Gardel cada día canta mejor'
Scene-painter of Buenos Aires — 'Sur', 'Barrio de Tango', 'Malena'
Tango's existentialist philosopher — 'Cambalache', 'Yira...Yira...', 'Uno'
Where D'Arienzo earned 'El Rey del Compás' — demolished 1960
Troilo's debut (1937), Biagi's debut (1938) — still operating in 2025
Three orquestas típicas daily — created the tanda format
Pugliese's 1946 masterwork — rhythmic concept with explosive stress
entities.definition: Onomatopoeia (YUM-ba, YUM-ba) for powerful stress on beats 1 and 3, with 2 and 4 played softly. Became tango's most dramatic signature.

entities.summary: Refrain singer — brief 30-second vocal chorus
entities.definition: Early tango singer format (c.1924-1937) where vocalist sang only a brief refrain, functioning as another instrument rather than featured performer.

entities.summary: Orchestra singer — integrated vocalist with dramatic weight
entities.definition: Evolution from estribillista (c.1937-1941) where singer became integrated member carrying dramatic weight, typically entering on second verse.

entities.summary: Buenos Aires slang — 5,000-6,000 words from Italian dialects
entities.definition: Argot of the lower classes of Buenos Aires featuring vesre (syllable reversal): tango→gotán, café→feca. Banned from radio 1943-1949.

entities.summary: Built franchise empire that industrialized ballroom tango — footprint diagrams, Bronze/Silver/Gold syllabus
Dance studio chain competing with Arthur Murray, emphasizing Hollywood glamour
Sanitized tango for American audiences — removed embrace, improvisation, 'objectionable' movements

entities.fullName: Rodolfo Alfonso Raffaello Pierre Filibert Guglielmi
entities.summary: Four Horsemen of the Apocalypse (1921) fixed tango-as-spectacle image in American imagination
Waldorf-Astoria bandleader 1933-1949 — commercial Latin music Americans thought was tango
Johnny Appleseed of tango — first BA tours, 80+ instructional videos, studied with Balmaceda
One of first authentic Argentine tango teachers in USA — LA from early 1970s, danced with Pugliese/Caló
198 performances at Mark Hellinger Theatre — Americans saw real tango for the first time
Arm's-length hold, head snaps, heel leads, strict-tempo music — nothing to do with Argentine tango
Tango Argentino cast member — discovered in obscurity, 278 lbs, flew to Paris on military cargo plane, sold out every show

The archetype of the cantor de orquesta; warm, intimate voice with porteño phrasing; partnership with Troilo defined Golden Age vocal style; key recordings: 'Malena', 'Garúa', 'Toda Mi Vida'; died in car accident in Mendoza

entities.nickname: El Ruiseñor de las Calles Porteñas
entities.summary: Sweet, charismatic voice; 'Los Dos Ángeles' partnership with D'Agostino produced ~93 RCA recordings; symbol of porteño phrasing in the 1940s; key recordings: 'Tres Esquinas', 'Ninguna'

entities.nickname: El Cantor de los Cien Barrios Porteños
entities.summary: Gynecologist turned explosive tango star; nasal, theatrical voice; 37 recordings with Tanturi; police blocked traffic when he performed; massive solo career; pioneer of tango-candombe fusion; key recordings: 'Así se Baila el Tango', 'Recuerdo'

THE voice of late tango; gravelly 'garganta con arena' (throat with sand); 26 recordings with Troilo; evolved into dramatic storyteller with rubato style; recorded 'Balada para un Loco' (1969); buried beside Troilo in Chacarita; sang at Tango Argentino world premiere
Pioneered deep bass voice in tango; 22 recordings with Troilo including 'Sur' (1948); founded El Viejo Almacén (1969); recorded Borges/Piazzolla poems (1965); defender of lunfardo

Sang with MORE major orchestras than any other singer; ~500 career recordings; clear, elegant voice; one of last surviving Golden Age singers (died at 91); key recordings: 'Nido Gaucho' (Di Sarli), 'Percal' (Caló), 'Garúa' (Laurenz)
Inventor of modern tango orchestration — 420+ works, National Tango Day named for his birthday
Found bandoneon's dark, singing voice — first professor of bandoneon
Gardel's lyricist partner — 'Volver', 'Por una cabeza', 'El día que me quieras'; died with Gardel in Medellín
Former boxer, saturated lyrics with lunfardo — 'Mano a Mano', Gardel recorded 21 of his songs
Lived to 99, Symbolist poetry influences — 'Anclao en París', 'Nostalgias'
Most famous tango ever — adapted ~2,700 times, closes virtually every milonga worldwide
With Ángel Vargas — definitive dance orchestra of the 1940s
De Caro school bandoneonist/bandleader — distinctive rhythmic style
Nuevo tango — 'music to listen to, not dance to'; split community into piazzolistas and antipiazzolistas; international success while rejected at home
Argentine rock movement that replaced tango as most popular music; captured youth while tango became 'grandparents' music'
Pugliese orchestra tradition — red carnation on piano as defiance symbol; Pugliese imprisoned by every successive regime
entities.definition: When Pugliese was imprisoned or couldn't perform, his orchestra played with a red carnation on his empty piano as symbol of resistance. Became tradition of solidarity.

entities.summary: Co-creator of 'Tango Argentino' (1983) with Héctor Orezzoli; scenic/costume designer; financed first production with father's life insurance; 'chic reo' (elegant roughness) aesthetic; Ciudadano Ilustre of Buenos Aires 2025
Co-creator of 'Tango Argentino' (1983) with Claudio Segovia; rescued forgotten milongueros from obscurity; died of heart attack in Manhattan at 38 with vision still unfolding
The dark years (1955–1983) when tango nearly died
entities.definition: Period from Perón's overthrow to democracy's return. Tango never explicitly banned but crushed through curfews, gathering restrictions, lunfardo censorship, and Peronist association. Milongueros stopped 20-30 years; orquestas collapsed from hundreds to single digits; mentor system destroyed overnight.

entities.summary: Pioneer of tango escenario; Ed Sullivan Show 1962; survived entire Decadencia performing professionally; choreographic advisor for Tango Argentino
Copes' partner for 30+ years; Tango Argentino lead; later independent career
Bridge ensemble through Decadencia; provided music for Tango Argentino show
Lived to 100; maintained duo with Ubaldo de Lío through Decadencia; co-founded Quinteto Real (1960)
The show that saved tango — Paris premiere Nov 11, 1983; Broadway Oct 9, 1985 (199 performances); cast flew on military cargo plane; sparked global revival

entities.nickname: La Voz de Oro del Tango
entities.summary: Operatic tenor with Italian bel canto influence; powerful voice contrasting Fiorentino's intimacy; key recordings: 'Uno' (1943), 'Cristal' (1944), 'Café de Los Angelitos' (1944)
Most natural, conversational singer of the era; 31 recordings with Troilo; 148 career recordings; key recording: 'Naranjo en Flor' (1944)
Joined Di Sarli at 16-17; warm, theatrical voice; ~46 recordings with Di Sarli; key recordings: 'Corazón' (1939), 'Charlemos' (1941)

entities.fullName: Juan de Dios Osvaldo Rodríguez Bonfanti
entities.summary: Rough, arrabalero voice; 130+ recordings with D'Arienzo; perfectly matched to D'Arienzo's rhythmic intensity; key recordings: 'Indiferencia' (1938), 'Trago Amargo' (1939)

Lyrical, Gardelian baritone-tenor; ~50 recordings with D'Arienzo; D'Arienzo slowed arrangements to accommodate his voice; banned from radio post-1955; key recordings: 'Dime Mi Amor' (1941), 'Tango Brujo' (1943)
Dramatic, passionate voice with Pugliese; 31 recordings; signature piece: 'Farol' (1943); voice functioned 'like a viola'; died in poverty
Sensual, bel canto voice; 48 songs with Pugliese; masterpiece: 'Pasional' (1951/52); extraordinary appeal to women
True cantora de orquesta with Canaro; 218+ recordings; mezzo-soprano; after affair with Canaro discovered, entered convent in Córdoba; lived in seclusion until death at 96
Founded DanceSport NYC (1985); provided space for Tango Argentino cast to teach; choreographed Al Pacino's tango in Scent of a Woman (1992)
Dance instructor at Stanford; founded Stanford Tango Week (1991-1997) — first major US tango festival; 32 instructors over its history
First Argentine tango instructor at Stanford (1991); settled SF 1988; continued teaching after husband Raul's death; launched Nora's Tango Week 1998
First major annual US tango festival; founded by Richard Powers; 32 instructors; essential catalyst for growth of Argentine tango in USA
Broadway show created by Luis Bravo (1990); 92-week SF run 1994; Broadway June 1997; featured Carlos Gavito; drew three couples from Tango Argentino cast
Stage tango master; Forever Tango star; minimalist theatrical style; 'We are painters. We paint the music with our feet.'
Most influential teacher of revival era; 'half the people you meet from the next generation were taught by Todaro'; codified eight-step basic; students include Zotto, Herrera, Mantiñán
Codified 'milonguero style' for North Americans (mid-1990s); Clarín: 'probably put more people on the dance floor than any other single teacher'
First venue in Europe dedicated exclusively to tango performance; godfather Julio Cortázar; meeting space for Argentine exiles during dictatorship; crucial for 1983 revival
Epicenter of 1913 tangomania; thés dansants three days per week; tango academy; Camille de Rhynal as chief instructor
Bandoneonist; arrived Paris 1920; formed house orchestra at El Garrón; with brothers maintained nightclubs that became 'Mecca of tango in Paris'
Investigation pioneer; studied with Tete; 'In one month-and-a-half I learned what I hadn't learned in two years' (on Naveira); repudiated 'nuevo' as style label (2009)
Villa Urquiza master; nickname from extraordinary foot rotation 'as if mopping the floor'; Carlos & Rosa Pérez continued his classes at Sunderland after his death
NYC pioneer; began 1991 with Trenner; studied with Naveira, Tete, Todaro, Pupi, Graciela González; built Dance Manhattan AT program 1994-2014; co-founded TangoMujer
Author of 'The Meaning of Tango' (2007); first non-Argentine to teach tango in Buenos Aires; built UK scene from early 1990s; documented male-only práctica system
Gavito's partner in Forever Tango; their 'A Evaristo Carriego' became one of most famous tango performances ever staged; trained by Antonio Todaro
Virulazo's partner; the slap on her fanny became their trademark (originally a spontaneous correction of misstep 20 years prior); Tango Argentino cast
Investigation co-founder with Naveira; ~12 years of 'choreographic analysis of the dance'; co-created CITA festival with Lola Díaz

Investigation leader; Cochabamba 444 prácticas 1987-1997; reduced all tango to three steps (cruce adelante, apertura, cruce atrás); studied with Pepito, Todaro, Virulazo, Portalea; explicitly rejected 'tango nuevo' as style label
'The feet of God' (NYT); The Tango Lesson star (1997); Libération: 'the best dancer in the world'; brought salon aesthetics to film
Founded Tango x 2 (1988); studied with Todaro and Finito; 'meticulous work of stylistic archaeology'; opened European academies
Trained by Pepito, Todaro, Graciela González; performed for Rolling Stones; danced with President Obama at 2016 state dinner; Guinness record highest-altitude tango
Created 'Dinzel System' — first systematization of tango dance structure; 3,600+ figure notation; taught both Zotto (stage) and Naveira (nuevo); authors of 'Tango: An Anxious Quest for Freedom'
T.M.E. (Tango Multiple Styles) methodology; co-founded TangoMeet.com (2011); 140+ cities in 35 countries; Honorary Itinerant Academic of National Tango Academy (2009)
Created and named multiple tango movements: ocho loco, sentada girada, elevador, el elástico; extended barridas/sandwichitos to calf/thigh level; possibly first to use 'Tango Nuevo' for dance
Youngest-ever Stanford Tango Week faculty; parents Mingo & Esther Pugliese (lineage from Petróleo); Alvin Ailey/Jacob's Pillow scholarships; co-founded Extempore Danse Company
'One tango' philosophy integrating nuevo principles into social tango; prolific YouTube educators; founded Project Tango nonprofit
Zotto's partner from 1985; co-founded Tango x 2 (1988); youngest couple in Tango Argentino cast (1986); background in modern dance
Naveira's partner from 1995; National Dance School graduate; co-founded Cosmotango and CITA; Boulder Tango Studio (2018 Best Academy)
Chicho Frumboli's partner from 2007; viral YouTube performances brought tango nuevo to millions globally
Birthplace of tango investigation movement; Naveira's weekly practica for 10 years; Club General Belgrano
'Mecca of Nuevo Tango'; peak nuevo practica scene; established 2004; closed as nuevo went 'vintage'
World's most important annual tango congress; co-founded by Naveira & Salas; now 26+ years running
Investigation Group member 1995-1997; contributed to development of universal teaching language for tango
Investigation Group; developed suspension concept and extended barrida vocabulary
Formed from ex-Pugliese musicians; survived Decadencia via Radio Municipal late-night broadcasts; still active
English-born; with wife Irene, sanitized tango for American audiences (1912-1918); published 'Modern Dancing' (1914)
Fashion icon, invented Castle Bob haircut; with Vernon, made tango 'respectable' by removing close embrace and improvisation

entities.fullName: Rodolfo Alfonso Raffaello Pierre Filibert Guglielmi di Valentina d'Antonguella
entities.summary: Gaucho tango scene in Four Horsemen of the Apocalypse (1921) fixed tango-as-exotic-spectacle image for generations
African American bandleader; Castles' music director; bridged ragtime and tango in early American dance scene
Forever Tango star; apilado embrace icon — 'tango is not a step, it is a feeling' — defined neo-traditional aesthetic
